title_en: Supplementary Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Measures for Litigation Fees of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Supplementary Provisions on the Measures for Court Litigation Fees

Fa Fa [1999] No. 21

(Adopted at the 1070th Session of the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court on June 19, 1999)

In light of the actual needs arising from the development of adjudicative work, and for the purpose of further regulating the court litigation fees and facilitating litigation by parties in accordance with the law, the following supplementary provisions are made to the Measures for Court Litigation Fees (hereinafter referred to as the "Measures"):

1. The "other litigation fees that the people's court deems should be borne by the party" as referred to in Article 4, Chapter I of the Measures shall specifically consist of the following:

(1) In non-property cases, the parties shall bear the actual expenses incurred for inspection, appraisal, announcement, and translation.

The burden of the above expenses shall be governed by the provisions of Article 19 of the Measures.

(2) In property cases and administrative cases, where a party genuinely has difficulty in collecting and providing relevant evidence on its own, and the people's court considers it truly necessary to conduct off-site investigation, evidence collection, and off-site mediation of the case, the travel expenses incurred in accordance with the standards prescribed by the State shall be borne accordingly.

The travel expenses incurred by the people's court during off-site investigation and evidence collection shall be borne by the party having the burden of proof, as determined by the people's court; the burden of travel expenses incurred during off-site mediation of the case shall be determined by the people's court.

2. Where a party applies to a people's court for enforcement of a legally effective judgment, ruling, mediation agreement, or payment order, the application enforcement fee shall be paid in accordance with the standard prescribed in Article 8(1) of the Measures. The application enforcement fee and the expenses actually incurred during enforcement shall be borne by the party against whom enforcement is sought that has refused to voluntarily perform the effective judicial document.

The expenses actually incurred during enforcement shall include: the travel expenses incurred by enforcement personnel of the people's court when conducting off-site enforcement of the case in accordance with the standards prescribed by the State; and the actual expenses incurred for inspection, appraisal, evaluation, auction, sale, storage, safekeeping, transportation, and other activities related to the enforcement of the case, carried out by the people's court or by other units or individuals commissioned by the people's court.

3. Subparagraphs (5) and (8) of Article 5, Chapter II of the Measures are amended as follows:

(5) For cases involving intellectual property disputes, if there is no disputed amount, the fee shall be RMB 500 to 1,000 per case; if there is a disputed amount, the fee shall be paid in accordance with the charging standards for property cases.

(8) For bankruptcy cases, the fee shall be calculated based on the total value of the bankrupt enterprise's property in accordance with the charging standards for property cases, and then paid at half of the calculated amount, provided that the maximum fee shall not exceed RMB 100,000.

4. Article 27 of the Measures is amended as follows:

If a party genuinely cannot pay the full amount of litigation fees on time due to financial difficulties, it may apply to the people's court for a deferment, reduction, or exemption. Whether to grant such deferment, reduction, or exemption shall be examined and decided by the people's court. Under any of the following circumstances, the people's court shall provide judicial assistance and decide, based on the specific circumstances of the case, whether the party may defer, reduce, or be exempted from paying litigation fees:

(1) The party is a public welfare institution, such as a welfare home, orphanage, nursing home for the elderly, rest home for disabled servicemen, mental hospital, or SOS Children's Village;

(2) The party is a disabled person with no fixed source of livelihood;

(3) The party's livelihood is difficult due to natural disasters or other force majeure, and the party is receiving state relief or finds it difficult to sustain production or operations;

(4) The party is receiving legal aid in accordance with relevant provisions;

(5) Any other circumstances under which the people's court considers that judicial assistance should be provided.

5. Article 28 of the Measures is amended as follows:

Article 28: For cases tried under the special procedures provided for in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, no case acceptance fee shall be charged. For cases tried under the trial supervision procedures provided for in the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the following provisions shall apply:

(1) Where a party applies for a retrial to a people's court in accordance with Article 179, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and the people's court, after examination, decides to conduct a retrial of the case, the party shall pay litigation fees in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Measures.

(2) Where a party did not appeal against the first-instance judgment or ruling of a people's court, and after the first-instance judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement has become legally effective, the party applies for a retrial, and the people's court, after examination, decides to conduct a retrial of the case, the litigation fees shall be paid in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Measures.

(3) For other cases that are brought up for trial or retried under the trial supervision procedures, no case acceptance fee shall be charged.

6. The charging of litigation fees by people's courts shall strictly adhere to the principle of "no fee without express provision". Except for the scope, items, and standards of fees expressly provided for in the Measures, these Supplementary Provisions, and the relevant judicial interpretations issued by the Supreme People's Court, no people's court at any level shall charge any other fees, and no other unit or individual shall charge any fees under the guise of litigation fees.

7. These Supplementary Provisions shall come into effect as of the date of issuance. For cases that have been concluded or enforced prior to the issuance date, no further recovery of related fees shall be made; for cases that have not yet been concluded or enforced, fees incurred after the issuance date shall be governed by these Supplementary Provisions; fees incurred prior to the issuance date shall be governed by the original Measures and the relevant provisions, and no further recovery shall be made.

(The Measures for Court Litigation Fees were formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation). These Provisions only make supplementary provisions on litigation fee issues that urgently need to be addressed. The Measures will be comprehensively revised in the near future based on the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.)

July 28, 1999
